svg.text: 🏦 LedgerCore — Complete Financial Transaction & Outbox Lifecycle
Synchronous Application Request Processing • Ownership Authorization • Atomic PostgreSQL ACID Commit • Transactional Outbox Persistence
🛡️ Zone 1: Client API, Auth & Ownership Boundary
⚙️ Zone 2: Service Layer & Business Rules Engine
🐘 Zone 3: PostgreSQL Atomic Database Transaction Boundary (@Transactional)
Prevents Mass-Assignment Vulnerabilities & Sanitizes Input Boundary
Prevents cross-customer account tampering & path-variable manipulation
IF Auth Failure ──► Throws AccessDeniedException (HTTP 403 Forbidden)
Both Source & Destination Accounts must be ACTIVE (FROZEN/CLOSED ──► 409 Conflict)
Transfer currency must match Account currency (e.g. INR == INR)
IF Balance < Amount ──► Throw InsufficientFundsException (HTTP 400 Bad Request)
Saved with status = PENDING inside the exact same DB transaction as financial state!
SELECT * FROM outbox_events WHERE status = 'PENDING' ORDER BY event_id FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
Polled every 5,000ms • Claims pending events without row lock contention • Status: PENDING ──► PROCESSING
Reliably hands off events to Apache Kafka streaming pipeline (ledgercore-transactions)
Enforced at the system boundary to prevent financial loss, lost updates, and dual-write anomalies
Authentication proves identity (`User`). Authorization verifies account ownership (`AccountAuthorizationService`).
Knowing an Account ID is never sufficient to execute a transaction.
Database advisory locks serialize duplicate network retries. JPA `@Version` rejects concurrent race conditions cleanly.
Network retry != permission to create duplicate financial transactions.
Every movement generates matching `DEBIT` and `CREDIT` entries in `ledger_entries`. Money is never spawned or deleted in isolation.
Provides an immutable, auditable log of balance history.
Financial state and outbox events commit together atomically. If DB transaction fails, outbox event rolls back cleanly.
Eliminates dual-write anomalies between database and Kafka.
